categories.main_business_segments: Eversource Energy is a public utility holding company operating through four primary business segments: electric distribution (serving approximately 3.3 million customers across Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire), electric transmission (operating high-voltage transmission infrastructure across New England), natural gas distribution (serving approximately 890,000 customers across Massachusetts and Connecticut), and water distribution (serving approximately 237,000 customers through Aquarion subsidiaries). The company also has an offshore wind business with a 50% ownership interest in projects being developed with Ørsted.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Eversource operates regulated utility infrastructure including electric transmission and distribution systems with substations, transformers, overhead and underground lines, natural gas distribution pipelines with storage and liquefaction facilities, and water treatment and distribution systems. The company owns 70 MW of solar power facilities in Massachusetts. Core operations involve purchasing and distributing electricity and natural gas to retail customers, with no generation assets except solar facilities, and managing water supply from owned surface water sources and groundwater supplies.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are residential, commercial, and industrial end-users across Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire. The company serves approximately 3.3 million electric customers, 890,000 natural gas customers, and 237,000 water customers. Customer segments include residential heating and cooling, small and medium commercial and industrial customers, large commercial and industrial customers, municipal customers, and fire protection services. Geographic markets are concentrated in New England with service territories in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire.
categories.geographic_coverage: Eversource operates primarily in New England, with service territories in Connecticut (CL&P serving 1.28 million customers in 149 cities and towns covering 4,400 square miles), Massachusetts (NSTAR Electric serving 1.47 million customers in 140 cities and towns covering 3,200 square miles; NSTAR Gas and EGMA serving natural gas customers in 117 communities covering 2,310 square miles), and New Hampshire (PSNH serving 535,000 customers in 211 cities and towns covering 5,630 square miles). Aquarion water utilities operate in 72 towns and cities across Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire, with approximately 92% of customers in Connecticut.
categories.supply_chain_position: Eversource operates as a midstream utility company in the energy supply chain, positioned between generation sources and end-use customers. The company purchases electricity from competitive suppliers and renewable energy facilities, purchases natural gas from upstream pipelines and storage facilities, and distributes these commodities to retail customers. The company does not own generation assets (except 70 MW of solar) and relies on third-party suppliers for energy commodities, which it passes through to customers without markup for standard service and default energy service.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include grid modernization and system resiliency improvements to address climate change impacts, expansion of renewable energy integration and offshore wind development (50% partnership with Ørsted on Revolution Wind, South Fork Wind, and Sunrise Wind projects totaling at least 4,000 MW potential capacity), electric vehicle infrastructure development, energy efficiency solutions, and emerging technologies such as energy storage and automation. The company is pursuing decarbonization initiatives including reducing Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions to achieve carbon neutrality by 2030 and setting science-based targets for Scope 3 emissions.
categories.revenue_model: Eversource generates revenue primarily through regulated utility rate structures approved by state regulatory commissions. Revenue comes from: (1) electric distribution charges including fixed customer charges and demand/energy charges; (2) electric transmission charges recovered through FERC-approved formula rates; (3) natural gas distribution charges including fixed charges and volumetric charges; (4) water distribution base rates with fixed and volumetric components; (5) energy supply pass-through charges (standard service, basic service, default energy service) where the company recovers costs without markup; and (6) various regulatory adjustment mechanisms and reconciliation charges for cost recovery. The company also generates revenue from renewable energy certificate sales from its solar facilities.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Eversource is a large regulated utility with a dominant market position in its service territories, holding exclusive franchises to distribute electricity, natural gas, and water in Connecticut, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire. The company faces competition from alternative energy sources, distributed generation, and energy efficiency solutions that reduce customer demand. In wholesale markets, Eversource competes with other New England utilities and independent power producers. The company is positioned as one of the largest utilities in New England with significant transmission infrastructure and is subject to FERC regulation alongside other New England transmission owners (NETOs) including National Grid and Avangrid.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Eversource is a large-cap utility with approximately $29.2 billion market capitalization as of June 30, 2022. The company earned $1.40 billion in net income ($4.05 per share) in 2022 compared to $1.22 billion ($3.54 per share) in 2021. Operating cash flows were $2.40 billion in 2022 versus $1.96 billion in 2021. The company maintains a strong credit rating (A- to A by S&P, Baa1 to A3 by Moody's) and projects long-term EPS growth in the upper half of a 5-7% range through 2027. Capital expenditures totaled $3.44 billion in 2022 with projected $21.52 billion investment from 2023-2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Eversource's value proposition centers on reliable energy and water delivery, system resilience and modernization to address climate change, integration of renewable energy and clean technologies, and customer service excellence. Differentiation includes: (1) significant transmission infrastructure investments improving grid reliability and enabling renewable integration; (2) commitment to decarbonization and carbon neutrality by 2030; (3) offshore wind development partnership providing clean energy generation; (4) grid modernization initiatives enhancing system resilience against extreme weather; (5) energy efficiency and electric vehicle infrastructure solutions enabling customer decarbonization; and (6) regulated utility model providing stable, predictable returns while serving essential utility services across three states.
